calls.summary: Dr. Sarah Whitfield called to explore a partnership with MB2 after reading the '20 Questions to Ask Before Selling' guide. Oscar walked her through the DPO model and how she keeps clinical and brand autonomy, then booked a practice valuation consultation for the following week. She left the call enthusiastic about preserving her autonomy.

Dr. James Okafor phoned asking how much his two-location practice was worth and requested a valuation. Lila explained the Practice Valuation and Transition Analysis process, reviewed P&L forecasting, and scheduled a consultation with the business development team. He was pleased with the clear next steps.

Dr. Emily Chen called about the digital marketing and SEO package to grow new patient volume at her practice. Rosey outlined the Google Ads, website, and online reputation offerings and booked a consultation to review a personalized marketing strategy. Dr. Chen sounded confident about moving forward.

Dr. Michael Torres, a first-time caller, reached out to schedule a partnership consultation after listening to the MB2 Underground podcast. Mary collected his practice details, ownership structure, and contact information, then confirmed an on-site assessment date. He booked the consultation and asked for the confirmatory diligence checklist.

Dr. Linda Park called with questions about provider credentialing turnaround before joining MB2. Lee described the Cerebro platform and re-credentialing tracking, then scheduled a consultation to map out her transition. She was reassured by the credentialing support timeline.

Dr. Robert Alvarez inquired about the procurement platform and how much he could save on lab and supply spend. Mike explained the 100-plus vendor network and negotiated discounts, then booked a consultation to review a spend analysis. Dr. Alvarez agreed to the follow-up meeting.

Dr. Nancy Feldman, an existing partner, called disputing a billing charge tied to her revenue cycle management collections statement. Jennifer reviewed the claim postings and opened a ticket with accounting to reconcile the discrepancy. No consultation was scheduled and the issue remained open pending review.

Dr. Paul Nguyen called to check the credentialing status of a new associate who had not yet been added to an insurance plan. Sue looked up the record in Cerebro but could not confirm the termination date and escalated to the credentialing team. Dr. Nguyen was frustrated by the delay.

Dr. Karen Boyd complained that her marketing campaign results had dropped and social media posts were late. Rose apologized, gathered the reporting details, and promised a callback from the marketing strategist. The concern was logged but no new consultation was booked.

Dr. Steven Marsh called about a procurement supply order that arrived incomplete and delayed a scheduled procedure. Oscar tracked the purchase on the platform and coordinated a replacement shipment with the vendor. Dr. Marsh remained unhappy about the disruption.

Dr. Amanda Reyes phoned to contest a billing amount on her monthly accounting and bookkeeping statement. Lila explained the payroll and accounts payable line items but could not fully resolve the dispute on the call. The matter was forwarded to finance for a second review.

Dr. Gregory Sund called upset about terms in his partnership shareholder agreement and wanted the legal team to revisit them. Lee documented the concerns and routed them to in-house legal for follow-up. No consultation was scheduled and the caller stayed dissatisfied.

Dr. Teresa Holloway called to cancel a scheduled facilities remodel due to budget concerns at her practice. Mike confirmed the cancellation and noted the CapEx project would be closed out. She declined any rescheduling and ended the call abruptly.

Dr. Victor Ramos called angrily disputing a valuation figure he received and claimed it undervalued his practice. Jennifer tried to explain the P&L methodology but the caller repeatedly interrupted. The call ended without resolution and a complaint was logged.

Dr. Olivia Hart reached voicemail after the queue overflowed and left a message about a delayed HR benefits enrollment for her staff. No agent answered the call and the message was captured for a callback. The enrollment concern was left unaddressed on this attempt.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes. The caller is an independent practice owner seeking to reduce administrative burden and overhead while retaining clinical autonomy and brand control, which is core to MB2's DPO value proposition.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller wants to understand how MB2's partnership model differs from traditional DSO models, specifically around maintaining practice autonomy and receiving comprehensive back-office support for a growing 8-person team.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus should have captured the caller's email address before closing and set clear expectations about what to expect during the consultation, such as discussing practice valuation and transition timelines.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling MB2 Dental. This is Marcus Bell speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, yes I'm calling because I've been hearing about MB2 and the whole partnership model you all promote. I'm a practice owner here in Atlanta with about eight dentists on my team and I'm just trying to figure out if there's a better way to run my business without losing control.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a great question and I'm glad you reached out. Many of our partners started exactly where you are. Let me get some information from you so I can make sure we're the right fit. What's your full name please?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's Dr. Robert Patterson.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you Dr. Patterson. And just to confirm, you're operating an independent practice right now in the Atlanta area?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, we've been independent for about twelve years now. We're in the 30306 ZIP code, north of the city.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. That's definitely within our service area. Tell me a little bit about what's driving your call today. What are some of the biggest challenges you're facing right now?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Honestly, it's the business side that's killing me. I didn't go to dental school to do accounting and HR and marketing. I want to spend more time with my patients and my team, not buried in spreadsheets. And I'm curious how a partnership would actually work without a DSO taking over my brand.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. That's why MB2 was created, to handle all those back-office functions so you can focus on patient care and growing your clinical team. Can you tell me roughly what your annual revenue is running right now?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We're doing about 2.2 million a year, and we've got decent profit margins, but the overhead is just exhausting.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's helpful context. We work with practices at all stages and revenue levels. Here's what I'd like to do. I'd love to get you on a consultation call with one of our partnership advisors who can walk you through exactly how the model works and show you what your cash flow and financial picture might look like partnering with us. Would you be available for a thirty-minute call next Tuesday at two PM?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Tuesday at two works for me. Yes, let's do it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. I've got you down for next Tuesday, October 29 at 2 PM. A member of our team will call you at this number to get started. Thanks for choosing MB2, Dr. Patterson, and we look forward to exploring this opportunity with you.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thanks, Marcus. I appreciate it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have a great day.

comment.text: Great structure and discovery, Marcus. You nailed the greeting, built rapport quickly, and got Dr. Patterson to open up about his real pain point: administrative overhead. One coaching note. Next time, grab the email address before the close so our follow-up team has it documented, and take 20 seconds to set expectations about what to prepare for the consultation call, like bringing last year's tax return or revenue reports. That small move makes the next interaction smoother.

qaPairs.question: What is a Dental Partnership Organization and how is it different from a DSO?
qaPairs.answer: A DPO like MB2 lets you keep your clinical and brand autonomy while we handle the business back office, unlike a traditional DSO that often centralizes control. A partnership consultation is the best way to see the difference for your practice, would you like to schedule one?

qaPairs.question: Can I keep my practice name and my clinical independence?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, doctors who partner with MB2 retain their brand, clinical decisions, and the way they run their practice. I can book a consultation with a partnership specialist to walk you through how autonomy works.

qaPairs.question: How much is my dental practice worth?
qaPairs.answer: Valuations are tailored to your P&L, collections, and growth potential, so we do not quote a set figure over text. Let me set up a consultation for a full practice valuation and transition analysis.

qaPairs.question: How do I sell my dental practice to MB2?
qaPairs.answer: The process starts with a conversation about your goals, followed by a valuation and a tailored partnership structure. I can schedule a consultation with our business development team to get you started.

qaPairs.question: What back office services does MB2 provide?
qaPairs.answer: We support accounting and finance, HR, compliance, marketing, procurement, revenue cycle, IT, legal, credentialing, and more through dedicated teams. A consultation can map these to your specific needs, shall I book one?

qaPairs.question: How many dentists are part of MB2?
qaPairs.answer: MB2 is the largest Dental Partnership Organization in the country with a community of more than 1700 dentists and over 500 support experts. I would be glad to book a consultation so you can learn what that network offers you.

qaPairs.question: Who founded MB2 Dental?
qaPairs.answer: MB2 was founded in 2007 and is doctor-led by CEO and Founder Dr. Chris Steven Villanueva. If you would like to hear more about the doctor-led model, I can arrange a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do I lose control of hiring and staffing?
qaPairs.answer: No, you continue to lead your team while our HR and talent acquisition teams support recruiting, benefits, and compliance. A consultation can show how this partnership works in practice.

qaPairs.question: What is the Carabelli Club?
qaPairs.answer: The Carabelli Club is part of our community and culture that connects partner dentists. I can share more during a consultation with our partnership team if you would like to book one.

qaPairs.question: Do you help with marketing and new patient growth?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our marketing team provides SEO, Google and Facebook ads, websites, reputation management, and patient recall systems. Let me book a consultation to review your growth goals.

qaPairs.question: Can MB2 help me open a brand new practice?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our facilities team manages de novo buildouts from floorplan design to equipment installation. I can set up a consultation to discuss your buildout plans.

qaPairs.question: How does MB2 handle billing and collections?
qaPairs.answer: Our revenue cycle team works with insurers to reduce claim denials and accelerate collections while improving your collection rate. A consultation can show how this would apply to your practice.

qaPairs.question: What is the onboarding process like after I partner?
qaPairs.answer: We provide hands-on integration support with documented planning guides plus virtual and on-site assessments. I can book a consultation to walk you through the transition.

qaPairs.question: Do you negotiate supply and lab costs?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our procurement team has relationships with more than 100 top dental vendors and an online purchasing platform with negotiated discounts. Let me schedule a consultation to review your supply spend.

qaPairs.question: Will I still be able to practice the way I want?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, preserving your way of practicing is central to our partnership model. A consultation is the best way to confirm how that fits your goals, would you like to book one?

qaPairs.question: Does MB2 offer continuing education?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer courses for dentists, hygienists, and team members covering restorative, cosmetic, leadership, and more. I can arrange a consultation to review the education options.

qaPairs.question: What legal support does MB2 provide?
qaPairs.answer: Our in-house legal team handles shareholder agreements, lease management, governance, contracts, and insurance claim defense. Let me set up a consultation to discuss your needs.

qaPairs.question: How long does a practice transition take?
qaPairs.answer: Timelines vary based on your goals and readiness, which is why we start with a personalized conversation. I can book a consultation so a specialist can outline a timeline for you.

qaPairs.question: Are there free resources I can review first?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer free tools like "20 Questions to Ask Before Selling" and "The Practice Transition Explained." I can send those and book a consultation whenever you are ready.

qaPairs.question: How do I get started with MB2?
qaPairs.answer: The best first step is a consultation with a partnership specialist to discuss your goals and next steps. I can find a day and time that works for you right now.
